messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: 'foreach' insteed of 'for loop'
parts:
Hi all

How can i apply 'foreach' insted of 'for loop' in my syntax. just note that i have 4 ' for loop'.

library(MASS)  
library(mirt)
library(psych)
library(doParallel)
#############################################################
itemrecovery <- function(sample.size, nitem, corr ,seed) { 
              # some codes in R
  }
core=detectCores()
registerDoParallel(cores=core-1)
myseed      <- sample.int(n = 1000000, size =3)
sample.size <- c(505, 1005, 2005)
test.length <- c(15, 30, 45) 
correlation <- c(0.0, 0.4, 0.8)
for (s in 1:length(sample.size)) { 
    for (t in 1:length(test.length)) { 
        for (k in 1:length(correlation)) {
            for (i in 1:length(myseed)){ 
                result[i,] <- itemrecovery(sample.size = sample.size[s], nitem = 
                test.length[t],corr=correlation[k],seed = myseed[i])   
            }
            result.m <- round(colMeans(result), 3) 
        }
    }
}

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: 'foreach' insteed of 'for loop'
parts:
Hi Balal

Did you have a look at the "Nesting Foreach Loop" document? See: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/foreach/vignettes/nested.pdf

It seems to describe nicely your problem, see the example code:

> x <- matrix(0, length(avec), length(bvec))
> for (j in 1:length(bvec)) {
+ for (i in 1:length(avec)) {
+ x[i,j] <- sim(avec[i], bvec[j])
+ }
+ }
>

x <-
+   foreach(b=bvec, .combine='cbind') %:%
+     foreach(a=avec, .combine='c') %do% {
+       sim(a, b)
+   }
x

messages.author: d0c629ef4df1de7c
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: 'foreach' insteed of 'for loop'
parts:
Hi Balal,

What should this code be doing? It must be the case that 'itemrecovery()' saves the results every time, because the R objects are written over in the loop iterations.

You may be better off using 'combn()' and 'parallel::mcmapply'.

Also be really careful with how you're using the seed- this doesn't look reproducible, and you may be reusing the same seed unintentionally.

Best,
Clark

Your code is:

#Run the loop and return the results across 100 iterations
foreach(s=sample.size, .combine = cbind) %:%
             foreach(t=test.length, .combine = cbind) %:%
                foreach(k=correlation, .combine = cbind) %:%
                  foreach(i=1:3, .combine = rbind) %dopar% {
result <-    itemrecovery(sample.size = sample.size[s], nitem = test.length[t],corr=correlation[k],seed = myseed[i])
}
write.table(result,"30%miss-2dim-data.csv", sep = ",", col.names =F, row.names = T,append = TRUE)

You're using both cbind and rbind inside the foreach. And assigning to result inside the body of the loop. With foreach you need to assign to the outside, ie.

result <- foreach(...

It's not clear what the code should be doing as it stands now.

core=detectCores()
registerDoParallel(cores=core-1)
myseed      <- sample.int(n = 1000000, size =3)
sample.size <- c(505, 1005, 2005)
test.length <- c(15, 30, 45) 
correlation <- c(0.0, 0.4, 0.8)
for (s in 1:length(sample.size)) { 
    for (t in 1:length(test.length)) { 
        for (k in 1:length(correlation)) {
            for (i in 1:length(myseed)){ 
                result[i,] <- itemrecovery(sample.size = sample.size[s], nitem = 
                test.length[t],corr=correlation[k],seed = myseed[i])   
            }
            result.m <- round(colMeans(result), 3) 
        }
    }
}
